La razón es simple: permite a dos desarrolladores codificar juntos, a distancia, sin perder la confidencialidad del código ni interrumpir los pipelines de CI/CD. En este artículo tienes una guía práctica (≈ 3 000 palabras) para entender su arquitectura, desplegarla en local y en la nube (AWS, GCP y Railway), y usarla con Node.js, Python y Rust. articles.title: LLM Evals Start as Thirty Test Cases, Not a Platform
articles.excerpt: You tweak a system prompt to fix one bad answer a user reported. You try it on that example, it looks great, you ship. Two days later someone notices the feature now ignores the output format half the…
articles.body: You tweak a system prompt to fix one bad answer a user reported. You try it on that example, it looks great, you ship. Two days later someone notices the feature now ignores the output format half the time, or started apologizing in every reply, or quietly stopped handling a whole category of input. Nothing failed in CI, because nothing in CI knew what "correct" meant. That is the gap evals fill. The word sounds like it needs a vendor, a dashboard, and a research team. It does not. The version that catches most regressions is a file of thirty or so real examples, a script that runs your feature against them, and a few assertions. You can write it this afternoon and grow it from there. Build the set from real failures The most useful eval set is not synthetic.

articles.body: Wrong but Real: Evaluating Intent-First Cypher Generation at 2,000 Properties (Ontographia Part 3) Series overview: Ontographia Teams that query a graph database such as Neo4j in natural language usually choose between letting an AI write the query and locking the system to handwritten templates. This series examines the common compromise (agent skills plus template selection) and proposes another split: the AI extracts a structured Intent, and an ontology-checked, deterministic pipeline compiles the Cypher ( Ontographia ). Part 1: The Graph AI Dilemma: Let LLMs Write Cypher or Suffer Template Maintenance Hell? . Production bottlenecks, research review, Intent-first hypothesis Part 2: The LLM Never Writes Cypher: Intent-First Design and Implementation .

articles.title: Counting the idle seconds: Bergson on the space hidden inside a clock
articles.excerpt: Every pane of the Mishe plant opens with a line like mind ok idle 9s. Refresh it and the number moves. It is the figure a reader looks at first, and the one most easily misread. The project's own docs…
articles.body: Every pane of the Mishe plant opens with a line like mind ok idle 9s . Refresh it and the number moves. It is the figure a reader looks at first, and the one most easily misread. The project's own docs found that it is not a per-mind figure. It reports the most recent activity anywhere in the plant, whichever mind acted last, and the correction on the docs now says so. The unit is the second, and a second is a clock interval. Henri Bergson spent much of Time and Free Will asking what a measured time costs us. His description of counting is exact enough to test against a plant.

articles.title: Building an ANPR Gate Pipeline: Triggers, Confidence and Events
articles.excerpt: Automatic number plate recognition (ANPR) looks like a camera problem, but in production it is mostly a pipeline and integration problem. Here is how a typical industrial gate setup is structured, fro…
articles.body: Automatic number plate recognition (ANPR) looks like a camera problem, but in production it is mostly a pipeline and integration problem. Here is how a typical industrial gate setup is structured, from the frame to the barrier. The pipeline Trigger – a loop detector, radar or motion zone signals a vehicle. Triggering avoids running recognition on every frame. Capture – an IR-illuminated camera with a short exposure captures the plate. Motion blur kills accuracy faster than low resolution does. Plate detection – a detector locates the plate region in the frame. Character recognition – OCR reads characters and returns a string plus a confidence score per character or per plate.

articles.title: Zero-Gas Autonomous Agents: Account Abstraction on Base L2
articles.excerpt: Autonomous agents broken by gas starvation are a chronic failure mode in crypto. If your LLM runtime or deterministic bot runs out of native ETH, execution halts instantly. Funding hundreds of sub-age…
articles.body: Zero-Gas Autonomous Agents: Account Abstraction on Base L2 Autonomous agents broken by gas starvation are a chronic failure mode in crypto. If your LLM runtime or deterministic bot runs out of native ETH, execution halts instantly. Funding hundreds of sub-agents with fractional gas amounts fragments capital, introduces operational overhead, and exposes private keys on hot instances just to sign raw transactions. The fix isn't complicated: run your agents through ERC-4337 Account Abstraction on Base (Chain ID 8453) using a Paymaster. The agent generates cryptographic intent via UserOperation ; a dedicated treasury subsidizes the execution. Zero native ETH touches the agent runtime.

This post is the workflow I use across Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Cursor and GitHub Copilot. It is tool-agnostic on purpose. If you want the VS Code setup walkthrough, I covered that in Using AI Agents in VS Code . This one is about habits. TL;DR Context is the budget, not the prompt.

articles.title: 5 bright planets to spot in November — when and where to see them
articles.excerpt: From a close encounter between Mars and Jupiter to dazzling Venus and elusive Mercury, November offers plenty of planetary highlights. Here's when and where to look.
articles.body: This is a great month for planet watching, either in the evenings or mornings. During convenient evening hours, the planet of choice is Saturn , visible well up in the southern sky during mid-to-late evening hours. Telescopically, the southern side of its famous ring system is currently tilted about 6½ degrees to our line of sight. Around the middle of the night, Mars and Jupiter come into view above the east-northeast horizon and just before the break of dawn are in excellent position, soaring high in the southern sky in the vicinity of the Sickle of Leo the Lion. Watch how Mars approaches Jupiter early in the month, passes it on Nov. 16, then spends the rest of the month sailing away to the east.

articles.excerpt: Jack Nicholson delivered mob cinema's ultimate statement of power.
articles.body: In crime cinema, a lethal line of dialogue can carry just as much weight as a loaded gun. Martin Scorsese's Goodfellas hooks audiences with Henry Hill's seductive declaration, “As far back as I can remember, I always wanted to be a gangster,” framing a life of crime as the ultimate aspiration. Miller's Crossing features Tom Reagan's wonderfully blunt take on underworld survival, while Casino , Scarface , and The Godfather overflow with dialogue that has long since bled into the cultural lexicon. Immortal phrases like “keep your friends close, but your enemies closer” and “an offer you can’t refuse” remain cinematic icons right alongside the actors and directors who brought them to life.

articles.body: Somewhere in Middle-earth, is there a Chili’s that serves orcs? Does an Uruk-hai host greet hungry customers, tell them it’ll be a 20-minute wait, and hand them a menu? Does the kitchen run out of manflesh halfway through the dinner rush? Is halfling served as an appetizer? What precisely is in the Triple Dipper? These are unreasonable questions to ask of an otherwise perfect fantasy epic. Unfortunately, The Lord of the Rings : The Two Towers invites every one of them with one line that feels deeply anachronistic.

articles.body: Abandoned, possessed, or infested spaceships in sci-fi films, books, and video games are usually not a welcoming place to hang your helmet and kick back inside. Many are distinctly marked as DO NOT APPROACH zones and equipped with clearly articulated warning messages to keep your distance, but that doesn't ever seem to stop scavengers, space pirates, or evil industrial mega corporations from waving off these dangerous signs to board anyway. Other creaky craft are apt to contain nasty alien hitchhikers or biological hazards not exactly conducive to a pleasant star-trekking voyage. Whether these nefarious neglected craft have just reappeared from the other side of a black hole or have been lying dormant for eons on a hostile planetoid, visitors are usually infrequent.

articles.excerpt: On Episode 234 of This Week In Space, Tariq Malik and Mike Wall are joined by Than Putzig of the Planetary Science Institute about a NASA-backed payload bound for the Marius Hills Pit on the moon.
articles.body: On Episode 234 of This Week In Space , Tariq Malik and Mike Wall are joined by Than Putzig of the Planetary Science Institute about a NASA-backed payload bound for the Marius Hills Pit on the moon. In our ongoing quest to develop a moon base, could we possibly utilize the area beneath the surface of the moon in order to make the moon habitable? Could Marius Hills Pit, a roughly 50-meter-wide opening that may lead into a lunar lava tube, become the Moon's first living habitat for humans? Putzig explains how geophysical instruments on a rover could detect hidden voids beneath the surface and measure the size of these lava tubes.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 31, 2015: Creepy skull-shaped Halloween asteroid flies by Earth, NASA names it the 'Great Pumpkin'
articles.excerpt: On October 31, 2015, an asteroid shaped like a human skull flew by Earth. Here's why it was so creepy.
articles.body: On October 31, 2015, an asteroid shaped like a human skull flew by Earth. It arrived with excellent timing on Halloween, which made the already-creepy asteroid even creepier. During its closest approach, the creepy asteroid was about 300,000 miles from Earth, or 1.3 times the average distance between Earth and the moon . So, it didn't pose a threat to our planet. It was discovered by astronomers at Hawaii's Pan-STARRS observatory only three weeks before the flyby, and it was given the official designation "2015 TB145." But no one knew what it looked like until the day before Halloween, when the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico captured the first radar images.

articles.title: Anthropic VS code extension on Cursor backdoored for nearly 12 hours
articles.excerpt: It's still unknown how attackers got access to Anthropic's verified Cursor account.
articles.body: An official extension for Anthropic’s Claude model was backdoored and threatened as many as 5,000 developers' machines, multiple sources reported Friday. Anthropic so far has yet to warn customers of the incident. The compromised package was a VS Code extension available in the marketplace of Cursor, a maker of AI-assisted developer tools, the company said Friday. The malicious version, 2.1.313, subsequently affected “at most 5,000 users,” presumably when they either downloaded it or their systems automatically fetched and installed it. Anthropic pushed version 2.1.314 several hours after the previous version became available on Cursor, according to independent researcher Kevin Beaumont.
